tier_reason: Peer-reviewed FAST '23 paper; the README abstract states up to 3.6x ext4-DAX throughput on concurrent workloads and 48% (YCSB/LevelDB) and 85% (TPC-C/SQLite) speedups over NOVA. Benchmark scripts are public (scripts/bench_st.py, bench_mt.py, bench_tpcc.py, bench_ycsb.py) and compilers are listed (GCC 10.3/11.3, Clang 14), but the CPU/PM hardware is only in the paper PDF (usenix.org blocked), so not A.

corrections.caveats: Numbers from the FAST 2023 paper abstract reproduced in the README; the paper PDF (usenix.org) was blocked, so hardware (Optane PM machine) and exact flags were not checked. Requires persistent memory (DAX) hardware to use. No LICENSE file (raw LICENSE 404, none shown on the repo page), so reference only. Last commit 2023-03-05.

notes: Numbers match README abstract exactly. usenix.org egress-blocked; a paper-access retier could check hardware for A (benchmark code public, compilers listed).

tier_reason: First-party hyperfine benchmark run by the project's own GitHub workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yaml, results in KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage-0.20.0-benchmarks); public code but CPU model not stated and not independent, so C, not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: pdu v0.20.0 vs du on the workflow's tmp.sample tree (hyperfine means): block-size 88.2 ms vs du --count-links 196.8 ms (2.23x), dust 110.9 ms (1.26x), gdu 168.4 ms (1.91x), ncdu 205.7 ms (2.33x), dua 231.0 ms (2.62x); with --deduplicate-hardlinks 88.3 ms vs du 196.9 ms (2.23x).
corrections.baseline: GNU du (also dust, dua, ncdu, gdu)
corrections.workload: Disk usage scan of a generated sample directory tree (tmp.sample) on a GitHub Actions runner, warm cache, measured with hyperfine; block-size and hardlink-deduplication modes among others.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark from the project's own CI workflow; GitHub Actions runner CPU model not stated; sample tree is small (~0.2 s for du). The 299.1 ms / 1255.2 ms and 1.061 s figures in the search record came from snippets of other releases and were not verified; replaced with the 0.20.0 report tables. Gain over du is from parallel traversal. Rust CLI, not a C++ library.

notes: Opened tmp.benchmark-report.competing.block-size.md and .deduplicate-hardlinks.md (raw) in the 0.20.0 benchmarks repo; claimed snippet numbers not on those pages, so replaced. License Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-08-09, 738 stars confirmed.

tier_reason: No openable page carries the claimed paper numbers (CHEOPS '23 and SYSTOR '22 PDFs on atlarge-research.com and dl.acm.org are egress-blocked; the artifact repo README has no numbers). The only openable numbers are an independent fio issue (#1206: io_uring 638k IOPS 4K randwrite on one core, P5800X Optane, kernel 5.9.16, vs SPDK perf about 2x on one core), which lacks a full methodology, so C pending a paper-access retier.

corrections.claimed_speedup: fio issue #1206 (independent user report): fio io_uring 4K randwrite iodepth 8 on one core reached 638k IOPS (2492 MiB/s) on an Intel P5800X Optane SSD while SPDK perf reached about 4000 MB/s on one core, roughly 2x per core (derived from page data). Paper claims from search snippets only, not opened: CHEOPS '23 (Ren and Trivedi) says io_uring is more than an order of magnitude less efficient than SPDK at high load (QD128, 7 devices); the record's 305 vs 171 KIOPS per core and 5 vs 13 cores figures (attributed to SYSTOR '22, Didona et al.) were not verified.
corrections.hardware: Intel P5800X Optane SSD, single core (fio issue #1206); CPU model not stated
corrections.caveats: Numbers only from an independent GitHub issue and from search snippets of the CHEOPS '23 / SYSTOR '22 papers (PDFs blocked). The CHEOPS '23 artifact repo https://github.com/atlarge-research/Performance-Characterization-Storage-Stacks has benchmark scripts but no numbers, hardware or flags in its README. SPDK requires dedicating cores to polling, hugepages and unbinding the NVMe device from the kernel; per-core wins come with 100% CPU busy-polling. Repo contains submodules with their own licenses.

notes: Strong candidate for a paper-access retier to B (CHEOPS '23 PDF at atlarge-research.com/pdfs/2023-cheops-iostack.pdf; SYSTOR '22 'Understanding modern storage APIs'). License BSD-3-Clause, last commit 2026-10-01, 3.7k stars confirmed.
